Each matchup is a binary relation between two institutions, forming a directed graph where nodes represent teams and edges denote contests. The strength vector for each institution is a derived quantity from historical win-loss records, normalized to a dimensionless scale. Temporal match states evolve through time, governed by these strength vectors and real-time game dynamics. These primitives form a dual framework: one rooted in discrete relational algebra (graph nodes), another in continuous stochastic modeling (strength evolution). Failure modes arise when data is sparse or inconsistent, leading to undefined or unstable mappings. The system exhibits duality between static relational structures and dynamic probabilistic models, enabling robust prediction under uncertainty.
